title: Crew voices and command radio
summary: The required tests pass: voices 29/29, smoke 5/5, syntax 544/544; command integration passes 8/8. Generated speech uses actual radio/spatial processing and push-to-talk controls live units through complete addressed calls. Historical failed diagnostics are retained below; aggregate totals include those failures.
reproduce: Set CHROME_PATH to /home/jayjay/.cache/chs/chrome.sh. From tools/, run node snap.mjs scenes/voices.mjs, then scenes/voicecommands.mjs and scenes/smoke.json with the same launcher. From the repository root: node tools/check.mjs syntax; node tools/voicebench.mjs; node tools/voicecommandbench.mjs. Open game/dev/voices.html through the game server for the listening preview.

changes.title: Crew dialogue through the actual audio graph
changes.change: Authored text was synthesized locally with the PC's installed SAPI voices. Radio words are band-limited and lightly saturated with generated keying/squelch; effects duck independently. Speaker identity has stable pitch, rate and timbre.
changes.observed: The lift screenshot shows separate chief, gunner and pilot subtitles. The voice scene exercised the Huey, command-board deployment, Marine contact/casualty calls, Hornet ball calls and urgent LSO wave-off. The isolated voice bus produced PCM with a peak of 0.1813 and zero overlapping utterances.
checks: 29/29 browser voice assertions; no page or console errors.
Rendered radio RMS: 0.00356 at 80 Hz, 0.0683 at 1 kHz, 0.00702 at 6.5 kHz.
19/19 asset and hook checks, including civilian/vehicle identity regressions added after the full scene.
limitations: Screenshots prove subtitle state, not intelligibility. The headless browser mutes hardware output.
The bank is 19.1 MiB compressed. Missing installed English voices or unavailable assets produce silent subtitles.
The full voice run precedes the final civilian/vehicle identity fix and last RADIO button position; targeted checks and later game runs cover those changes.

media.caption: Huey leaving the carrier, with the chief, gunner and pilot identified in the subtitle feed.
Standalone listening room: generated speech produces PCM and exposes speaker, channel, distance and wall controls (2/2 checks).

changes.title: Local combat voices and interruption
changes.change: Nearby Marines speak from live positions. Distance and wall/door intersections change gain and low-pass filtering. Urgent calls stop lower-priority sources; pause, OFF and out-of-range events cancel real audio.
changes.observed: The contact image shows Marines near the landed Huey and a contact/corpsman subtitle. Separate audio checks move a listener, insert a wall, interrupt a line and stop the voice bus.
checks: Live distance fading, wall low-pass, out-of-range cancellation and radio-only mode passed.
Pause/OFF, zero volume, queue age/bounds and no-system-voices silence passed.
limitations: The scene positions units and delivers deterministic hostile-shot and field-care events through game hooks. It does not validate autonomous combat tactics.
Wall acoustics approximate obstruction, without diffraction, room reverberation or carrier roll/pitch transforms.

media.caption: Scripted Sandbar encounter: the subtitle feed includes a nearby contact and a corpsman call.

changes.title: Speak an addressed order
changes.change: Hold F9, say the called station, THIS IS COMMAND, one supported order, OVER, then release. The live roster lists callers and capabilities; typed calls use the same parser. Units reply WILCO/OUT or UNABLE with their existing voice identity.
changes.observed: A controlled final microphone transcript waited for release, then changed a real Marine squad to hold. A typed call then ordered that squad to defend Sandbar. Invalid procedure and paused-game calls did not mutate orders.
checks: 38/38 parser, recognition lifecycle and dispatch checks, including ambiguity, cancellation, permission/network errors, stale units and SAY AGAIN without repeating the action.
limitations: Recognition was driven by a test provider. A physical microphone, accents/noise and remote browser speech services need manual testing.
This is a bounded military command-net convention, not a validator of every legal aviation transmission. Only listed unit orders are supported.
Browsers may send microphone audio to their own speech service; the panel discloses this before use.

media.caption: The command radio panel displays the complete call and the addressed squad's acknowledgement.

changes.title: Regression checks and retained failures
changes.change: The required smoke scene remains intact. Failed diagnostic runs are retained alongside passing results and explained in the findings document.
changes.observed: Smoke screenshots show the carrier start and the helicopter climbing above its scripted 40 m starting altitude. Earlier failures exposed stale listener/parking assumptions, casualty-fixture ambiguity and a browser termination during screenshot capture.
checks: Smoke 5/5 with no browser errors; syntax 544/544 modules.
Earlier 24/31 and 28/29 runs, and a terminated screenshot run, are failed evidence, not passing validation.
limitations: SwiftShader software rendering at 45% resolution; no performance improvement is claimed.
A veteran phrase review, subjective voice listening and physical headset/XR controls remain manual checks.

limitations: All work stays on ngc/look-voices in the requested worktree. No merge, push or publication.
Character dialogue uses conservative period vocabulary; the newly requested spoken-order grammar is not restricted to 1980.
